note: NY-close read, Fri 2026-11-20 (~3:01 PM CT, Investing.com live quotes). Dollar eased off Thursday's 19-month high — DXY 103.79 (-0.05%) — as the AI-stock rout deepened (S&P -2%, Nasdaq -3.5%, 7th straight down day) and haven flows lifted the yen most: USD/JPY 158.50 (-0.75%), still below 160. Gold crashed to a fresh 14-month low near $3,503 intraday, closing $3,523.55 (-2.81%) — worst week in eight months (~-9%). Yields fell hard on the haven bid (2Y 4.62%, -15.6bp; 10Y 4.92%, -12.7bp) and Dec Fed hike odds slipped to 89.8% (CME FedWatch, 3:01 PM CT) from 96.5% at the NY open after UoM 1-yr inflation expectations cooled to 3.7% (from 4.3% prelim). Oil rebounded late — Brent $92.82 (+0.91%), WTI $83.94 (+1.82%) — on fresh Houthi strikes on Riyadh and the Saudi evacuation order for Hodeida, though both stay on track for a third straight weekly loss. AUD weakest after the jobs miss (0.6615, -0.66%, near a one-year low); USD/CAD 1.4351 (+0.07%), back near the 52-week high. Spot levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices.
